# Code Review — Story 8.1: Unit Tests for Numeric Column Right Alignment

**Story:** `epic-8/8.1-unit-tests-numeric-column-right-align` (TDD RED phase)
**Change under review:** one new test file + story-doc status flip
- `apps/dms-material/src/app/shared/components/base-table/base-table-numeric-alignment.spec.ts` (new, 3× `it.skip`)
- `.github/workflow-output/implementation-artifacts/stories/epic-8/8.1-unit-tests-numeric-column-right-align.md` (`in-progress` → `done`, Completion Notes added)

**Review method:** three independent read-only layers run concurrently — (L1) spec quality + TDD red-phase correctness, (L2) project context + build/test wiring, (L3) cross-cutting concerns. Findings below are consolidated; severities re-verified against the actual CI pipeline before classification.

**Verdict: APPROVE WITH CHANGES.** No blockers to merge — the file is convention-consistent and inert today (all tests skipped). Two majors should be resolved or explicitly accepted by the story owner before Story 8.2 unskips, because both bite at the red→green handoff, not now.

---

## Blockers
None.

> Note: L1 initially flagged line 22 as a blocker (TS2344 generic-constraint violation). Re-verified against CI: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs only `pnpm nx affected -t lint build test`. `build` uses `tsconfig.app.json` (excludes specs), `test` is vitest/esbuild (strips types, no typecheck), and ESLint does not report TS2344. So the error is **latent**, not a current-CI failure → reclassified to Major below.

## Major

### M1 — Generic constraint violation at line 22 (latent type error)
`base-table-numeric-alignment.spec.ts:22` declares `ComponentFixture<BaseTableComponent<Record<string, unknown>>>`, but the component's generic is constrained `T extends { id: string }` (`base-table.component.ts:60-61`). Under `tsc -p tsconfig.spec.json` this is `TS2344: Type 'Record<string, unknown>' does not satisfy the constraint '{ id: string; }'`.

- **Why it matters:** Not caught by current CI (see note above), but any future typecheck/lint-tsc step on spec files fails here. Sibling specs use concrete row types (`base-table-mat-table.spec.ts:27-29` → `BaseTableComponent<{ id: string; name: string }>`).
- **Fix:** declare a local row interface (e.g. `{ id: string; qty: number; price: number; name: string; lastTrade: string }`) and use it as the generic arg. One-line change, do now while the file is fresh.

### M2 — AC #2 under-delivered vs the story's written acceptance criterion
The story's AC #2 promises a **computed-style** assertion that numeric cells resolve right-aligned **and** that non-numeric body cells do *not* resolve to it. The delivered test (`:155`) only asserts the SCSS rule exists with `flex-end` or `text-align:right`; there is no computed-style check and no explicit negative on non-numeric alignment.

- **Why it matters:** As written, AC #2's second half was dropped. This is a real deviation from the acceptance criterion, not just an implementation detail.
- **Mitigating (self-documented):** The Completion Notes explain jsdom does not apply component SCSS into the DOM (computed styles resolve empty), so the test asserts source text instead — and deliberately leaves `flex-end` vs `text-align:right` open for Story 8.2 to choose. This is a reasonable adaptation, but it means the *written* AC is not met; the story owner should confirm they accept asserting rule-existence in lieu of computed-style + negative.
- **Suggested:** either (a) update the story's AC #2 text to match what was actually delivered, or (b) add a non-numeric negative assertion (`expect(numericCellRuleBody())` does not apply to `.dms-body-cell` without the modifier) so the "non-numeric does NOT resolve" half is at least covered structurally.

## Minor

### m1 — SCSS-source parser can produce false-red against a correct 8.2 implementation
`numericCellRuleBody()` (`:105-129`) matches only an exact **column-0** `.dms-body-cell--numeric {` line and inspects only that top-level block's body by brace-depth. Two brittle cases:
1. If 8.2 writes `&.dms-body-cell--numeric` nested under `.dms-body-cell`, or indents the rule, the parser throws `'block not closed'` / fails red even though the CSS works.
2. If 8.2 puts `text-align:right` in a more specific selector (e.g. `.dms-body-row .dms-body-cell--numeric { ... }`), the test stays red despite working CSS.

- **Why it matters:** The red→green signal is valid *only* if 8.2 adds a top-level, column-0 rule with `flex-end`/`text-align:right` directly in that block. That constraint is documented in the comment (`:98-103`) but the failure message itself never hints at it — an implementer hitting red gets "expected a rule in base-table.component.scss" with no pointer to the column-0 requirement.
- **Mitigating:** This is not novel over-coupling — it's a verbatim copy of the established Story 5.x convention (`headerCellRuleBody()` in `base-table.component.spec.ts:104-127` does the identical thing for `.dms-header-cell`, and that test went red→green successfully).
- **Suggested (optional, deferrable to 8.2):** extend the expect message to "…as a column-0 top-level rule", or loosen the parser to also accept an indented/nested occurrence of the class name.

### m2 — AC #1 coverage gap: boolean/actions/custom column types untested
`columns` covers text/number/currency/date only, but `ColumnDef.type` also has `'boolean'`, `'actions'`, `'custom'`. If 8.2 adds `.dms-body-cell--numeric` to any of those, all three tests still pass (false green).

- **Why it matters:** Only if the AC is broader than "number/currency only". Acceptable as-is if the story strictly scopes numeric alignment to number+currency — confirm against the story text.
- **Suggested:** add one `boolean` column and assert it does *not* carry the class, closing the gap cheaply.

### m3 — Misattributed convention comment (line 12)
Header says "same convention as `base-table-mat-table.spec.ts`" for asserting SCSS source instead of computed styles. That file does **not** read SCSS via `readFileSync` — its only style assertion is `getComputedStyle(headerRow).position === 'sticky'` (`:228`). The actual source-reading precedent is `base-table.component.spec.ts:97`.

- **Why it matters:** Misleading pointer for a future reader; the spec's own "Story 5.x" phrasing elsewhere (`:44`, `:152`) cites it correctly, so line 12 is internally inconsistent.
- **Fix:** point line 12 at `base-table.component.spec.ts` (or just say "the Story 5.x convention").

## Nits

### n1 — Duplicated fixture helpers
`nextFrame()` (`:51-53`) is a verbatim copy of `base-table-mat-table.spec.ts:22-24`; the `clientHeight=570` stub (`:60-70`) duplicates that file's `:52` and `:447` (which already contains two internal copies). No shared test util exists in dms-material. YAGNI — leave as-is; extract only if a 4th copy appears.

### n2 — Story-doc Task 3.1 wording drift
Doc says each test gets a "TODO(Story 8.2) comment"; the spec has only the eslint-disable marker (which does say "Story 8.2 removes the skip…"). Functionally equivalent, textually not as promised. Cosmetic.

## Confirmations (verified, no issue)
- **Red-phase convention consistent.** All three skips use `it.skip(` + `// eslint-disable-next-line vitest/no-disabled-tests -- BLOCKED: intentionally disabled TDD RED phase test; Story 8.2 removes the skip…` — byte-for-byte identical to `base-table.component.spec.ts:411/420/426`, `open-positions.component.spec.ts:313`, and `file-upload-validation.spec.ts`. Not novel.
- **Red is genuine.** No assertion passes under the current component (no `.dms-body-cell--numeric` class, no such SCSS rule). The 2-failed/1-passed probe claim in Completion Notes matches the assertions.
- **Nothing runs today.** All tests skipped → vitest fires no `beforeEach`/`afterEach`; cost is one small file read at collection plus module import. No leak risk now; when 8.2 unskips, setup mirrors the proven `base-table-mat-table.spec.ts:42-57` pattern (clientHeight=570 stub + one real animation frame), which already proves body rows render under it.
- **Discovery confirmed.** `apps/dms-material/vite.config.mts` include glob `{src,tests}/**/*.{test,spec}.{js,mjs,cjs,ts,mts,cts,jsx,tsx}` matches the file; no exclude. Root `vitest.config.ts` lists only server/electron projects — no double-run.
- **`__dirname` + `readFileSync` safe.** jsdom env but CJS globals work in vitest-transpiled specs; identical precedent ships and passes in same dir (`base-table.component.spec.ts:97-98`, `environment.electron.spec.ts:31`). Blast radius if it ever broke: this suite only (vitest isolates each spec into its own module context).
- **Fake-timer isolation justified.** `vi.useFakeTimers()` at `base-table.component.spec.ts:182` (paired with `useRealTimers()` in afterEach); separate file = separate vitest module context.
- **Placement/naming fits.** Siblings in same dir: `base-table.component.spec.ts`, `base-table-mat-table.spec.ts`; the suffix-named variant pattern matches. Coverage unaffected (`base-table.component.ts` already in coverage exclude list; no source named `base-table-numeric-alignment.*`).
- **AC #3 met.** Header guard with non-empty check (`headers.length > 0`) — passes today by design, matching the doc's note that header cells never carry the class.
- **No public API / build output change.** Spec-only file; no barrel/index references it; Angular build excludes `.spec.ts`; vitest picks it up for tests only (intended).
